name: Blackwater peat swamp
analogue: Borneo's peat swamp forest (Sebangau, Central Kalimantan; Belait, Brunei): tea-black water, stunted forest, the closest air

name: East coast (the Padomaic shore)
analogue: A windward monsoon coast (the Malabar coast in the south-west monsoon; Sabah's east coast in the north-east monsoon): wind, long swell, overcast and rain off the ocean, silver sea haze

name: South coast (the Sea of Mists)
analogue: Borneo's south coast and the Sundarbans' creeks: sea mist most mornings, warm milky haze over mangrove and mud

name: West coast (Topal Bay)
analogue: A sheltered bay coast facing the sunset (Kerala's lagoons at Alappuzha, Sabah's west coast at Kota Kinabalu): sunny mornings, sea breeze, squalls, fiery sunsets over the water

name: Green marsh and backwater
analogue: Kerala's backwaters and Kuttanad's paddies; Borneo's open freshwater marsh: bright green reed and paddy under a luminous white sky

name: Highland and mesa
analogue: The Western Ghats (Munnar, the Nilgiris), Borneo's karst and montane uplands (Mulu, Kinabalu's lower slopes): crisper air, blue layered distance, valley mist below

name: Islands
analogue: Small tropical islands in clean sea air (the Lakshadweep, Sabah's offshore islands): bright light, turquoise shallows, passing showers, the clearest air

name: Lowland swamp rainforest
analogue: Borneo's lowland dipterocarp forest (Danum Valley, Sabah): closed canopy, green dim light, steam off the canopy at dawn, afternoon thunderstorms

name: River corridor
analogue: The Kinabatangan and Rajang in Borneo, the Periyar in Kerala: brown rivers in a humid valley, river fog at dawn, storms in the afternoon
